title: Install Tremplin
description: Install Tremplin step by step with local assets, an npm tarball, or published packages.
lead: Add Tremplin to your project with a package manager, CDN, or local source files.

sections.heading: Install
paragraphs: This checkout is Tremplin 0.8.0-beta.0, an unreleased development version. Start with local assets or a locally packed tarball; these instructions do not establish that a public npm or CDN release exists.

For a separate application, first build the framework and run npm pack as described under Download. Copy the generated tarball into that application’s vendor/ folder, then choose your package manager below. Install both positioning and calendar peers. Do not install the package into its own framework checkout.

code.source: npm install ./vendor/tremplin-0.8.0-beta.0.tgz @floating-ui/dom vanilla-calendar-pro

sections.callout: Follow the npm guide or Vite guide for a consumer application. To work on this documentation website instead, follow Build from source below. The framework repository and a consumer application have different startup commands.

sections.heading: Using npm
paragraphs: Import the root namespace when you need several plugins, or use named root exports such as Tooltip, Toast, and Popover. Individual component subpaths export their component as the default. Your bundler resolves the package exports and shared chunks; do not copy an individual chunk in isolation.

The example target must exist before calling a component method. Root imports register the core data APIs; a focused component import registers its own data API. Optional adapters and Tremplin extensions are separate from the core.

code.label: Application entry after the target markup exists
code.source:
import 'tremplin/css'
import * as tremplin from 'tremplin'

tremplin.Collapse.getOrCreateInstance('#welcome')

code.label: Named root imports
code.source: import { Tooltip, Toast, Popover } from 'tremplin'

code.label: Individual component entry (alternative to the root import)
code.source:
import 'tremplin/css'
import Collapse from 'tremplin/collapse'

Collapse.getOrCreateInstance('#welcome')

rows: Core CSS, Sass, and native component entry points. Optional adapters and extensions are retained in the repository, not shipped in the core package.

sections.callout: Use @floating-ui/dom for positioning and vanilla-calendar-pro for Datepicker. See JavaScript for lifecycle and disposal, and Browsers and devices for support targets. On Windows, use npm.cmd if PowerShell blocks npm.ps1.

sections.heading: Using Yarn
paragraphs: For a consumer application using Yarn Berry, choose the node-modules linker if your tools do not support Plug’n’Play. Copy the locally packed archive into vendor/ before installing. Run the application’s own development script afterward; do not assume every project has a yarn start command.

code.source:
yarn config set nodeLinker node-modules
yarn add ./vendor/tremplin-0.8.0-beta.0.tgz @floating-ui/dom vanilla-calendar-pro

sections.callout: Keep the framework repository’s npm lockfile and use npm ci when building Tremplin itself. After a release has actually been published and verified, registry installation becomes npm install tremplin@0.8.0-beta.0 @floating-ui/dom vanilla-calendar-pro.

sections.heading: More packages
paragraphs: Tremplin currently supports a local npm-compatible tarball and compiled local assets. This project does not provide official RubyGems, Composer, or NuGet packages. Do not assume a similarly named registry package belongs to Tremplin.

sections.heading: Using RubyGems
paragraphs: There is no official Tremplin gem. In a Rails or other Ruby application, use your JavaScript asset pipeline or copy the compiled distribution into public assets. Preserve the relative CSS, JavaScript, and icon paths shown in the local HTML workflow below.

sections.heading: Using NuGet
paragraphs: There is no official Tremplin NuGet package. In ASP.NET, place the compiled distribution under wwwroot and reference it from your layout, or use an npm-based frontend build. PHP applications can also serve those assets directly; there is no official Tremplin Composer package.

sections.heading: CDN
paragraphs: The following version-pinned jsDelivr example is a publication template, not the recommended installation for this unreleased checkout. Use it only after verifying that the exact package version exists and its files match the trusted local integrity manifest.

All browser downloads are ES modules, using Tremplin’s module loading contract. Floating UI and Vanilla Calendar Pro are included in the bundle. The standard build leaves those dependencies external and requires a bundler or import map. Load one runtime owner; no browser build creates a window global.

code.label: After verified publication only
code.source:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tremplin@0.8.0-beta.0/dist/css/tremplin.min.css"
  integrity="sha384-CRpCUZ98QhvAAv1ISSsLbdBxrBta9WkDWgphsIpursF+3Y7FVuXd6nr0lxRj9For" crossorigin="anonymous">
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tremplin@0.8.0-beta.0/dist/js/tremplin.bundle.min.js"
  integrity="sha384-ROwsTH/s8vKy4wUpGDtBM4Ufl6II2+BNdCLMdUDOHz1SxkqqxG1WSNYOfzxV8kbM" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

sections.heading: Using CDNs
paragraphs: Pin the complete version instead of latest. Keep integrity and crossorigin="anonymous" on cross-origin stylesheet and script requests. When an asset changes, update its URL and matching SHA-384 value together.

The stylesheet references a calendar icon relative to its CSS directory. Preserve the distribution’s css/, js/, and icons/ layout when self-hosting. A Content Security Policy must permit the stylesheet, script, and image origins you actually use; do not disable CSP to fix a path error. Focused builds are listed in Package contents.

sections.heading: Alternative CDNs
paragraphs: After npm publication, an npm-backed provider such as unpkg may offer the same versioned files. No cdnjs listing is currently provided by this project. Check the version and bytes against a trusted release manifest; a CDN hostname is not proof that a package is official.

code.label: Compute the SHA-384 value locally
code.source: openssl dgst -sha384 -binary tremplin.bundle.min.js | openssl base64 -A

sections.callout: Security warning: compare the same algorithm, version, and file. If its SHA-384 differs from the trusted manifest, do not load it or disable integrity checks. See the Download guide for a cross-platform Node.js verification example.

sections.heading: Download
paragraphs: Use compiled assets for a no-build HTML page, or build and pack the repository for a separate bundler application. Local downloads work without registry publication. The consumer tarball is not a complete documentation-site checkout; use this repository to develop the framework or website.

rows: Use the stylesheet, browser bundle, and calendar icon linked above. Keep their directory layout. No Node.js is needed for the plain HTML page.
Sass, TypeScript, tests, and documentation live in the framework repository. Install development dependencies, build, and pack locally as below.

sections.heading: Use local assets
steps: Copy dist/css/, dist/js/, and dist/icons/ into a dist/ folder beside your application’s index.html. For the self-contained bundle, the three linked assets suffice. Separate dependency modules are not part of core dist. Preserve dist/LICENSE, and dist/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt with redistributed assets.
Copy the complete document below into index.html. Serve the folder over HTTP through XAMPP or another local server.
Select “Show details”. The panel should expand and the trigger should expose its expanded state. Select it again to close the panel. Check keyboard focus and the browser console.
paragraphs: For the standard ESM alternative, bundle the installed peer dependencies yourself, or download the documentation-only Floating UI and Calendar Pro modules into a separate vendor/ directory. These demo-support files are not core package exports. Preserve their notices. Add the import map before any module script.

code.source:
Hello, Tremplin!

Build your first responsive interface.

Your framework is working.

code.label: Standard ESM alternative with separately supplied dependency modules
code.source:
<script type="importmap">
{
  "imports": {
    "@floating-ui/dom": "./vendor/floating-ui.js",
    "vanilla-calendar-pro": "./vendor/vanilla-calendar-pro.js"
  }
}
</script>
<script type="module">
  import { Collapse } from './dist/js/tremplin.js'
  // This module runs after parsing: #welcome must exist.
  Collapse.getOrCreateInstance('#welcome')
</script>

sections.callout: Load one complete framework stylesheet and one ES module runtime. The bundle is self-contained; tremplin.min.js requires the import map below. Never mix independently built standard, minified, bundled, or optional-extension runtimes. Root and component entries from the same unminified graph share instances.

sections.heading: Build from source
paragraphs: Use the Node version required by this checkout and its installed tools. In the framework repository, install the lockfile dependencies, build the framework, and create a local package tarball. Publishing remains blocked; npm pack creates a local archive and is not a release approval.

code.label: Framework repository
code.source:
npm ci
npm run build
npm pack

code.label: Separate consumer application (adjust the path)
code.source: npm install ../tremplin/tremplin-0.8.0-beta.0.tgz @floating-ui/dom vanilla-calendar-pro

code.label: Documentation website, from the framework checkout after building
code.source:
npm run site:prepare
npx astro dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4321

sections.callout: Keep the server terminal open and visit its printed URL, normally http://127.0.0.1:4321/. Use npm.cmd and npx.cmd in Windows PowerShell if execution policy blocks the .ps1 launchers. Do not run a second development server on the same port.

rows: Use local downloads or a locally packed tarball until the exact public release is verified.
Build and pack the framework first, copy the archive into the consumer vendor/ folder, and check its versioned filename.
Unstyled page or missing calendar arrows
Check Network requests. Preserve dist/css and dist/icons, including the relative SVG URL.
Check the browser script request, unique target ID, data-trm-target, and console. Use btn-solid or btn-outline rather than retired button classes.
Use only one runtime owner. Remove independently built module copies. Reuse one exact module URL and its shared graph.
Start the server in the right folder; keep its terminal running and use the printed host and port.

sections.heading: For AI tools & LLMs
paragraphs: Give coding assistants the machine-readable documentation index, API reference, and relevant component guides. The AI guide explains project conventions. Tremplin does not currently distribute an agent-skills package or llms-full.txt; do not use an unrelated installer as a Tremplin installer.

title: AI guidance
description: Give coding assistants accurate Tremplin documentation and component contracts.
lead: Ground generated interfaces in this framework’s actual version, markup, and source contracts.

sections.heading: 1. Supply project context
paragraphs: Point your coding tool at the repository README, llms.txt, component guides, and generated API reference. In a local checkout, include metadata/components.json and the relevant src/js/ module.

code.label: Example prompt
code.source:
Build a responsive settings form using Tremplin 0.8.0-beta.0.
Use unprefixed CSS classes and data-trm-* behavior hooks.
Follow the local Forms, Collapse, and Dialog guides.
Use visible labels, keyboard-operable controls, and explicit error text.
Use local dist assets until registry publication is verified.
Do not introduce another framework or invent Tremplin APIs.

sections.heading: 3. Review generated markup
steps: Check every class against the component guide and every method against the generated API.
Keep IDs unique, associate labels and errors, and verify target selectors.
Prefer native controls. Treat generated HTML and suggested dependencies as unverified until reviewed.

sections.heading: 4. Run the relevant checks
paragraphs: Use your application’s build and browser checks. Framework contributors should run the repository checks below. A generated page still needs a keyboard and screen-reader review.

code.source:
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run test:csp
npm run check

sections.callout: Tremplin currently provides llms.txt, source metadata, and documentation. This project does not publish an agent-skills package or llms-full.txt; do not use an unrelated installer as a Tremplin installer.

title: Approach
description: Understand Tremplin’s HTML, CSS, Sass, and JavaScript conventions.
lead: Build from semantic HTML, add responsive classes, and introduce JavaScript where interaction requires it.

sections.heading: 1. Start with the document
paragraphs: Include a doctype, document language, UTF-8 encoding, and viewport metadata. Reboot sets predictable base styles, including border-box sizing; review existing application CSS before adopting it.

code.source:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My project</title>
</head>
<body>...</body>
</html>

sections.heading: 2. Build mobile first
paragraphs: Unqualified classes define the small-screen layout. Breakpoint variants add changes at larger widths; they do not require a second mobile stylesheet.
sections.example:
First column
Second column

code.source:
First column
Second column

sections.heading: 3. Separate appearance and behavior
paragraphs: Public classes such as btn, card, and row define appearance. data-trm-* attributes configure behavior. Framework events use names such as shown.trm.collapse. Avoid loading frameworks with overlapping unprefixed selectors together.

rows: Runtime colors, font stacks, component tokens, and subtree themes.
Generated scales, breakpoints, utilities, feature switches, and compiled customization.
Project-specific composition; load it after the framework and keep selectors deliberate.

sections.heading: 5. Prefer native semantics
paragraphs: Use buttons for actions, anchors for navigation, labels for inputs, and native dialog elements for Dialog and Drawer. Add CSS-only components without JavaScript. Use the typed plugins when state, focus, positioning, or lifecycle behavior is needed.

sections.heading: 6. Extend deliberately
paragraphs: Keep optional extensions separate from core imports, use logical start/end directions, and check dark mode, reduced motion, keyboard access, and reflow. Read Package contents before selecting a focused build.

title: CSS variables
description: Apply Tremplin runtime tokens globally, per component, and in light or dark themes.
lead: Change visual tokens in ordinary CSS without rebuilding the framework.

sections.heading: 1. Load your overrides last
paragraphs: Link your application stylesheet after Tremplin. Inspect the computed variables in browser developer tools before changing a token.

code.source:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="./assets/tremplin.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="./app.css">

sections.heading: 2. Override root variables
paragraphs: Set a foreground color alongside its background token. Existing explicit light/dark theme selectors can override root values, so include your selected theme in global brand overrides.

sections.heading: 3. Tune an individual component
paragraphs: Set component variables on a custom class rather than changing every button.

code.source: <button class="btn brand-button" type="button">A custom button</button>

sections.heading: 4. Select a color mode
paragraphs: Use data-trm-theme="light", dark, or auto. Automatic mode follows the operating system. A theme switcher should offer an understandable choice and preserve the user’s selection.

code.source: document.documentElement.dataset.trmTheme = 'dark'

sections.heading: 5. Know the boundary
paragraphs: CSS variables cannot be substituted directly into media-query conditions. Change generated breakpoint values and spacing maps through Sass instead. Some components define their own local variables, so consult that component’s variables table when a root override has no effect.

rows: Primary semantic color and contrasting text.

sections.heading: 6. Verify the result
steps: Test text and control contrast in every theme you expose.
Keep a visible keyboard focus indicator.
Check components inside themed subtrees as well as at document level.
paragraphs: Continue to the detailed customization reference and color modes guide.

title: JavaScript
description: Use Tremplin’s browser bundle, ESM imports, data APIs, lifecycle events, and cleanup.
lead: Add interaction with declarative attributes or typed component instances. CSS-only pages do not need a script.

sections.heading: 1. Choose a distribution

rows: ES modules: standard minified build requires peers; bundle includes them. Neither creates a global.
ESM package imports for bundlers; declarations are included.
Available for tooling, but interactive components require a browser DOM.

sections.callout: Browser builds use the Tremplin ES-module contract. Use type="module". The standard build needs Floating UI and Vanilla Calendar Pro resolved by your bundler or import map; the bundle includes both. See Install for a complete local import map.

sections.heading: 2. Use the data API
sections.example: This example uses the installed browser bundle.

code.source: Project details

paragraphs: Use unique target IDs and one behavior toggle per trigger. Component modules register their own data handlers when loaded. Plain text attributes are not a safe way to configure sanitizer callbacks.

code.label: Bundler application after the target exists
Browser module: use instead of another runtime script

sections.heading: 4. Handle lifecycle events
paragraphs: Register listeners before changing state. Pre-change events can be canceled with preventDefault(); completion events indicate the finished transition. A canceled or overlapping operation may not emit a completion event.

sections.heading: 5. Dependencies and frameworks
paragraphs: Install @floating-ui/dom for package-based positioning components such as Menu, Tooltip, and Popover. The browser build includes it. Tremplin Datepicker is implemented locally and does not require Vanilla Calendar Pro.

sections.heading: 6. Dispose when removing DOM
paragraphs: In React, Vue, or another renderer, initialize core plugins after mount and dispose before removing their elements. Avoid having both a renderer and a plugin independently own the same state. Experimental adapters remain in the repository but are not exported or installed by the core package; use the core lifecycle directly.

code.source:
// Run during application teardown, before removing #details.
Collapse.getInstance('#details')?.dispose()

sections.heading: 7. HTML safety and CSP
paragraphs: Tooltip and Popover sanitize HTML by default. Keep sanitization enabled; supplying DOM elements or custom sanitizers makes the caller responsible for their safety. Under Trusted Types enforcement, permit the private tremplin policy.

code.source: require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types tremplin

sections.callout: These two directives cover Trusted Types only, not a full CSP. See SECURITY.md in the source package for the complete tested baseline. Provide external application scripts or a deliberate nonce strategy under a strict script policy.

sections.heading: 8. Without JavaScript
paragraphs: Typography, grid, tables, cards, and other presentational styles continue to work. Script-driven disclosures and overlays need a usable fallback: keep essential content reachable and do not make critical tasks depend on a hidden, uninitialized panel.

title: Browsers and devices
description: Understand Tremplin’s browser targets, test coverage, and device limitations.
lead: Target modern browsers and verify the devices your application actually supports.

sections.heading: 1. Read the support target

rows: Current major version; verify on real devices.
Internet Explorer and legacy embedded browsers

sections.callout: These are Tremplin project targets, not proof of testing every listed version. Automated tests use the locally installed Playwright Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit engines. WebKit automation does not replace testing Safari on Apple devices.

sections.heading: 2. Check platform requirements
paragraphs: The compiled styles use logical properties, custom properties, container queries, and color-mix(). Plugins use modern JavaScript, native dialog behavior, IntersectionObserver, and pointer events where relevant.

code.source:
const features = {
  dialog: typeof HTMLDialogElement !== 'undefined' &&
    typeof HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal === 'function',
  observer: 'IntersectionObserver' in window,
  containers: CSS.supports('container-type', 'inline-size'),
  colorMix: CSS.supports('color', 'color-mix(in srgb, red, blue)')
}
console.table(features)

sections.heading: 3. Test input and viewport changes
steps: Exercise keyboard, mouse, touch, and zoom workflows.
Check narrow widths, landscape orientation, software keyboards, and safe-area padding.
Verify reduced-motion and forced-color settings, scrolling overlays, and focus restoration.

sections.heading: 4. Separate build requirements
paragraphs: A static page using compiled assets does not require Node.js in the browser. Package metadata declares Node.js 20 or newer for the toolchain; check the engine requirements of Vite, Astro, and other tools you choose as well.

sections.heading: 5. Handle older environments
paragraphs: Do not claim compatibility based only on JavaScript transpilation. CSS features and native dialog behavior also matter. Define your application baseline, feature-test critical paths, and supply an application-specific fallback or an understandable unsupported-browser message.

title: Accessibility
description: Apply semantic markup, labels, focus, contrast, and assistive-technology checks with Tremplin.
lead: Accessible components are a starting point. Your content, customization, and complete workflows still need verification.

sections.heading: 1. Understand the limits
paragraphs: The project targets WCAG 2.2 AA and uses automated browser and axe checks. Passing them is not a conformance certification. Manual screen-reader and real-device validation is still pending for final release sign-off.

sections.heading: 2. Structure and label your page
steps: Use landmarks and a logical heading hierarchy, and provide a skip link where navigation repeats.
Use visible labels for controls; placeholders are supplementary hints.
Give informative images useful alt text and hide purely decorative icons.
Use native buttons for actions and anchors for navigation.

sections.heading: 3. Associate instructions and errors
sections.example: Use an address you can access.

code.source:
Use an address you can access.

Enter a valid email address.

paragraphs: After a failed submission, expose a useful error summary and guide focus to it when appropriate. Server-side validation is still required.

sections.heading: 4. Preserve focus and overlay behavior
paragraphs: Give Dialog and Drawer a visible title referenced by aria-labelledby. Test initial focus, Tab and Shift+Tab, Escape, nested surfaces, and restoration to the opener. Never place required form input inside a tooltip.

code.source:
Help

Use the form labels to complete each field.

sections.heading: 5. Check color, motion, and hidden content
paragraphs: Do not communicate errors, availability, or status by color alone. Verify text and control contrast after customization. Respect reduced motion and avoid removing focus outlines. Use .visually-hidden for supplementary screen-reader text, not for focusable controls that remain invisible.

code.source: Loading results…

sections.heading: 6. Validate a complete journey
steps: Complete the task with the keyboard, including error recovery.
Test at 200% zoom and at a narrow viewport without losing content.
Review announcements and focus with NVDA on Windows; add VoiceOver and other combinations required by your audience.
Run automated checks and record browser, assistive technology, result, and remaining issues.
paragraphs: Read the W3C WCAG quick reference for success criteria and testing guidance. Automated checks do not replace these manual steps.

title: Download
description: Download built Tremplin assets, source packages, and integrity metadata.
lead: Choose ready-to-use browser files or build from source; verify that the version and bytes match.

rows: You want a plain HTML setup without a build process.
You need declared package exports, Sass sources, types, or bundler imports.
You are developing Tremplin or building its documentation and release assets.

sections.heading: 2. Download compiled files
paragraphs: Use the Release assets table below. For most pages, download tremplin.min.css and tremplin.bundle.min.js. CSS-only pages can omit JavaScript. Focused CSS bundles are alternatives for narrower use cases; avoid importing both full and focused builds unnecessarily.

sections.heading: 3. Build a source checkout

code.source:
npm ci
npm run build
npm run check
npm pack

paragraphs: These commands run from the framework repository. Keep the lockfile. npm pack creates a local package without publishing it. The website build and contributor scripts are not part of the consumer package contract.

sections.heading: 4. Verify integrity
paragraphs: Download integrity.json alongside the files. Compare its version and SHA-384 digest with your downloaded bytes. A digest served from the same compromised location is not an independent trust guarantee; retain a trusted manifest for release verification.

code.label: Save as verify.mjs; run node verify.mjs next to integrity.json

sections.heading: 5. Install and verify in the browser
paragraphs: Follow the complete Installation document example, inspect Network requests, and toggle the sample disclosure. The generated downloads below are available from this local documentation build; they do not imply that a public registry release has been published.

title: Package contents
description: Choose Tremplin CSS builds, JavaScript formats, types, and source entry points.
lead: Understand which files to ship, which files need a bundler, and which files are source-only.

code.source:
tremplin/
  dist/
    css/          full, grid, reboot, and utilities CSS; minified variants
    js/           ESM, CommonJS facades, chunks, declarations, source maps
    integrity.json
  src/scss/       Sass modules and optional extensions
  src/js/         TypeScript components and utilities
  icons/          sprite and icon CSS
  themes/         runtime theme presets
  starters/       HTML, Vite, React, and Vue starting points
  metadata/       component and API contracts
  docs/           project and migration documentation

rows: Configurable Sass entry; must be compiled.

sections.heading: 3. Select JavaScript

rows: Standard ES module; positioning and calendar peers remain external.
Self-contained ES module including both peers; no window global.
Canonical native ES modules; Node 24 also supports require(ESM) interop, not a separate CommonJS build.
Explicit canonical module path in the same graph.

sections.callout: The standard browser ES module has bare package dependencies, not split browser chunks. Use the self-contained bundle in plain HTML, or provide a bundler/import map for the standard build. Individual js/dist modules intentionally retain their sibling module imports.

sections.heading: 4. Keep declarations and maps straight
paragraphs: TypeScript declarations describe the API and are resolved through package exports; they are not browser scripts. Source maps support debugging and can be deployed or withheld according to your application policy. Source TypeScript and Sass are inputs, not compiled browser assets.

sections.heading: 5. Verify package contents locally

code.source:
npm pack --dry-run
npm run test:package

paragraphs: Run these in the repository. The tarball consumer check verifies installation and exports. Prefer declared package subpaths instead of internal chunks, which may change between builds.

title: Bundlers
description: Set up Tremplin with Vite and understand Sass, package imports, and peer dependencies.
lead: Use Vite for a small working application, or adapt the same package exports to your existing build system.

sections.heading: 1. Create an application folder

code.source:
mkdir my-tremplin-app
cd my-tremplin-app
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev vite

paragraphs: Use a Node.js version supported by your chosen Vite release. Run these in a separate application folder, not in the framework repository.

sections.heading: 2. Install Tremplin
paragraphs: For the current checkout, build and pack Tremplin first, then install its tarball with the path adjusted for your directories. After a registry release is verified, the package name can replace the tarball path.

paragraphs: Merge these scripts into the application package.json. Open the URL printed by Vite and test the Details button; then build and preview the production output.

sections.heading: 6. Optional Sass customization
paragraphs: Install Dart Sass, create app.scss, and import that file from main.js instead of importing the compiled CSS.

code.source: npm install --save-dev sass

code.label: app.scss
main.js CSS replacement

sections.heading: 7. Webpack and other bundlers
paragraphs: Use the same declared package imports. Configure your existing tool’s CSS and Sass processing and install the Floating UI peer. Browser-native ESM cannot resolve bare package specifiers without additional resolution; plain HTML can use the self-contained ESM bundle with type="module", or a standard build with the Install guide’s import map. This guide provides a complete Vite recipe, not a tested configuration for every bundler.

sections.heading: 8. Production review
steps: Confirm emitted CSS and JavaScript requests succeed from the deployed base path.
Check only the components and optional adapters you use are imported.
Test interactions after minification, keyboard access, and content without JavaScript.
Run your application tests; use Tremplin’s contributor check only when developing the framework itself.

title: RTL
description: Enable right-to-left interfaces with Tremplin logical properties and one stylesheet.
lead: Use the document direction and language to adapt layout without a separate RTL build.

code.source:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="ar" dir="rtl">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="./assets/tremplin.min.css">
  <title>مثال Tremplin</title>
</head>
<body>...</body>
</html>

sections.heading: 2. Prefer logical utilities

rows: Drawer placement relative to writing direction.

sections.example:
واجهة تدعم اتجاه الكتابة

hello@example.com

sections.heading: 4. Isolate mixed-direction content
paragraphs: Wrap addresses, identifiers, and code in an appropriate dir="ltr" container, or use <bdi> for an unknown-direction value. Preserve logical DOM reading order; do not reverse elements merely to imitate visual RTL.

code.source: البريد: hello@example.com

sections.heading: 5. Test directional interactions
steps: Verify drawer placement, menu positioning, horizontal navigation, and Datepicker arrow keys.
Check nested mixed-direction regions, focus order, and reading order.
If an application changes language at runtime, retest or recreate affected plugin instances so cached positioning and direction state are refreshed.
sections.callout: The same stylesheet supports both directions. RTL styling does not translate your text, labels, date locale, or icon meaning; those remain application responsibilities.
